mainEntity.name: How much does junk removal cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each job is priced at one flat rate in writing after a survey of the full scope — there is no rate card and no published hourly price. The industry mostly prices by truck volume, and published guide ranges for that model are in "Junk removal, explained" above, labeled as industry figures. Our price for your job is the written flat rate for your job.

mainEntity.name: How is the flat rate set?

acceptedAnswer.text: We review the full scope of each job — the items, the distance, the manpower, and the equipment — and give a flat rate, as opposed to an hourly rate. Access found at the survey (stairs, long carries, a hot tub to section) is inside the price, not added on the day.

Furniture, appliances, mattresses and box springs, electronics, exercise equipment, hot tubs, yard debris, renovation debris (drywall, lumber, flooring, cabinets, fixtures), bagged household junk, and whole-property cleanout contents from homes, estates, evictions, and businesses.

mainEntity.name: What items can you not take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hazardous and regulated waste: wet paint and solvents, fuels and motor oil, pesticides and household chemicals, pressurized tanks, asbestos-containing material, lead paint material, and medical or biohazard waste. Those belong to licensed handlers and household hazardous waste routes.
Yes. The tub is drained and disconnected from power and water before the appointment; the crew then cuts the shell and hauls it out in sections.

mainEntity.name: Do you take refrigerators and other appliances?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — washers, dryers, ranges, dishwashers, refrigerators, freezers, and water heaters. Appliances that contain refrigerant are routed to processing where certified technicians recover the refrigerant before the appliance is processed, as federal rules require.

mainEntity.name: Do you do estate and eviction cleanouts?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — whole-property cleanouts for estates, evictions, foreclosures, and turnovers, surveyed as one scope and priced at one flat rate for the whole property.

mainEntity.name: Do you take construction or renovation debris?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — drywall, lumber, flooring, carpet, cabinets, countertops, and fixtures from renovation work. Dense material such as concrete, brick, and soil is planned by weight, because weight governs how much a truck can carry in one load.

mainEntity.name: What happens to my junk after pickup?

acceptedAnswer.text: The load is sorted before anything is thrown out. Usable goods are routed toward donation, recyclable materials toward recycling, regulated-stream items toward the facilities that handle them, and only the remainder goes to a transfer station or landfill.

mainEntity.name: What if the junk includes a safe or a piano?

acceptedAnswer.text: Those are not forced through junk removal. A gun safe or another high-mass asset of 1,500 to 3,500 lbs moves under Structural Integrity Relocation (SIR), with floor deflection analysis to L/360; a piano moves under the piano, antique and white-glove service. Ask about the piece when you request your quote and it is routed to the right service.

mainEntity.name: How do I get a flat rate quote for junk removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Get My Flat Rate Quote — Short (Quick Quote) by default, or Detailed Project, switching in place with From, To, and What's moving preserved. The pill button reads "Get a flat rate quote". Or use the free film-only video walkthrough survey room, where a person makes the estimate from your film.
